epics.title: Core Experience and Identity
epics.jtbd: When a visitor lands on the site, I want to immediately understand the author's focus and have clear ways to contact them, so that I can explore their work or get in touch.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: LCP < 2.5s and CLS < 0.1 across all viewports
epics.tocConstraintRef: Frontend rendering pipeline and asset delivery network bandwidth
requirements: R1: Implement a high-end scrollytelling narrative interface presenting materials with absolute authenticity.
R2: Exclude all traditional studio photography, substituting high-fidelity typography and document presentation.
R3: Ensure the interface is fully usable and responsive on mobile viewports.
R4: Implement WCAG 2.1 level AA accessibility compliance across all scrollytelling views.
R5: Display an Imprint (Impressum) reachable from every page.

slices.title: Scrollytelling UI Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend for this epic, I want to build a scrollytelling interface without studio photos, so that the Core Experience and Identity outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a visitor navigates to the root path
When they scroll down the viewport
Then the narratives transition smoothly with typography in place of studio photos
Given a mobile device viewport
When the scrollytelling interface loads
Then text contrast is at least 4.5:1 and an Imprint link is visible in the footer
slices.tocConstraintRef: Browser render thread blocking during scroll events

slices.title: UI Accessibility and Regression Testing
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify mobile layout and accessibility compliance, so that the Core Experience and Identity outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the scrollytelling page is deployed
When an automated accessibility scanner runs
Then zero WCAG 2.1 AA violations are detected
Given the scrollytelling page is deployed
When a visual regression test runs
Then traditional studio photography is verifiably absent from the rendered DOM

epics.title: Podcast Media Hub
epics.jtbd: When a visitor wants to listen to the podcast, I want to browse episodes with detailed show notes and audio playback, so that I can consume the audio content directly.
epics.tocConstraintRef: Database lookup time for episode metadata
requirements: R1: Provide a media player optimized for clean audio playback without relying on studio imagery.
R2: Expose a podcast episode API endpoint providing metadata and audio URLs.
R3: Define the relational schema for podcast episodes.

slices.title: Podcast Episode Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the database schema for this epic, I want to define tables for podcast metadata and audio URLs, so that the Podcast Media Hub outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a pristine PostgreSQL database
When the podcast Flyway migrations are executed
Then an episode table is created with audio_url and metadata columns

slices.title: Podcast Episode API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the shared contract for this epic, I want to define the episode DTO, so that the Podcast Media Hub outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a need to synchronize backend and frontend
When the episode DTO is requested
Then a TypeScript interface defining the episode metadata and audio_url is available

slices.title: Podcast Episode Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to serve episode data, so that the Podcast Media Hub outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given existing podcast episodes in the database
When the episode list endpoint is requested via GET
Then a 200 OK response returns the metadata and valid audio URLs

slices.title: Podcast Audio Player UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the UI for this epic, I want to provide a clean audio player, so that the Podcast Media Hub outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the podcast episode endpoint is active
When the visitor triggers the play button on an episode
Then the audio element streams cleanly without displaying any studio imagery

slices.title: Podcast Delivery QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to test the full audio playback lifecycle, so that the Podcast Media Hub outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a test environment with seeded podcast episodes
When a synthetic user accesses the podcast hub
Then the audio playback control is fully keyboard operable and plays the seeded audio

epics.title: Public API for External AI Agents
epics.jtbd: When an external AI agent operates on behalf of a user, I want it to securely read documentation, place service orders, and send direct messages, so that the user can seamlessly hire me or contact me through their personal assistant.
requirements: R1: Provide an autonomous A2A infrastructure allowing external agents to query the author's materials.
R2: Enforce authentication on the A2A endpoints using API keys.
R3: Return deterministic, machine-readable JSON responses designed for AI ingestion.

slices.title: A2A Security Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the database schema for this epic, I want to define storage for API keys, so that the Public API for External AI Agents outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a pristine PostgreSQL database
When the A2A API key Flyway migrations are executed
Then an api_keys table is provisioned with secure hash columns

slices.title: A2A Materials Endpoint
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to expose authentic materials as JSON, so that the Public API for External AI Agents outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid API key provided in the Authorization header
When an external AI agent queries the materials extraction endpoint
Then a 200 OK response returns the structured authentic materials
Given an invalid API key
When the endpoint is queried
Then a 401 Unauthorized response is returned

slices.title: A2A Integration Testing
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to test agent interactions against the A2A infrastructure, so that the Public API for External AI Agents outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the A2A infrastructure is deployed
When an integration test attempts to fetch materials with and without valid keys
Then it strictly verifies 200 and 401 behaviors respectively

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
requirements: R1: Goal: Measure if the site successfully drives interest in the author's work and materials.
R2: Question: Are external AI agents actively consuming the A2A infrastructure? Metric: Weekly unique agents successfully calling the API.
R3: Question: Are human visitors completing the scrollytelling path? Metric: Scroll depth completion rate per session.

slices.title: Telemetry Ingestion Backend
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to process event metrics, so that the Platform Telemetry and Measurement outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an incoming telemetry payload for an A2A consumption event
When the POST ingestion endpoint is hit
Then the metric is persisted to the timeseries datastore
Given an incoming payload for scrollytelling depth
When it is processed
Then the progression metric is correctly incremented

slices.title: Telemetry Accuracy Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to ensure metric precision, so that the Platform Telemetry and Measurement outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a synthetic user traversing the scrollytelling path
When the session concludes
Then the telemetry database reflects the accurate depth completion rate
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero discrepancy in test metric counts

epics.title: Initial Content and Acceptance
epics.jtbd: When receiving the delivered system, I want to see it populated with realistic content, so that I can verify all paths and features work end-to-end.
requirements: R1: Seed the platform with authentic scrollytelling copy and layout definitions.
R2: Seed at least one valid podcast episode with a working audio file reference.
R3: Seed initial API keys and demonstration materials for the A2A infrastructure.

slices.title: Initial Content Flyway Seeding
slices.jtbd: When implementing the database schema for this epic, I want to inject real foundational data, so that the Initial Content and Acceptance outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the application starting against a fresh database
When the seeding migrations run
Then the system is populated with realistic authentic materials, one audio podcast, and one demo API key

slices.title: End-to-End Content Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to confirm content renders on all paths, so that the Initial Content and Acceptance outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the deployed instance loaded with seeded content
When an E2E acceptance test traverses the primary paths
Then all links resolve correctly without placeholder lorem ipsum content

epics.title: Privacy Consent Management
epics.jtbd: When a visitor arrives on the site, I want to be asked for consent before any non-essential trackers load, so that my privacy preferences are respected and the site complies with ePrivacy regulations.
epics.tocConstraintRef: Consent state evaluation block on page load
requirements: R1: Capture opt-in consent before any non-essential telemetry or tracker loads (GDPR/ePrivacy).
R2: Ensure refusing consent is as easy as accepting.
R3: Provide a mechanism to revoke consent later with equal friction.

slices.title: Consent Banner UI Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend for this epic, I want to capture user consent choices, so that the Privacy Consent Management outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a first-time visitor arriving at the site
When the page loads
Then a consent banner blocks non-essential trackers until explicit opt-in is granted
Given a visitor has granted consent
When they navigate to their privacy settings
Then they can easily revoke their consent with equal friction
slices.tocConstraintRef: Client-side storage lookup for consent flag
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero UI layout shifts from banner injection

slices.title: Consent Blocking QA Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify trackers remain blocked without opt-in, so that the Privacy Consent Management outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh browser session
When the user dismisses the consent banner without opting in
Then no telemetry or external network calls are fired

epics.title: Data Subject Rights and GDPR Compliance
epics.jtbd: When a user whose personal data was submitted by an AI agent requests access or deletion, I want to be able to export or erase their data within the statutory deadline, so that the system complies with privacy regulations.
requirements: R1: Provide a backend mechanism to export all telemetry data for a specific IP or agent identity.
R2: Provide a mechanism to permanently erase a subject's data upon request within 30 days.

slices.title: GDPR Export and Erasure Service
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to orchestrate subject data removal, so that the Data Subject Rights and GDPR Compliance outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a verified request from a data subject
When the erasure service is triggered
Then all personal identifying metrics and IP data are hard-deleted

slices.title: Erasure Protocol Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to guarantee total deletion, so that the Data Subject Rights and GDPR Compliance outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a populated telemetry database
When an erasure operation is performed for a specific subject
Then a subsequent SQL assertion proves zero residual identifying rows exist
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% assertion pass rate for data absence

epics.title: Data Protection and Recovery
epics.jtbd: When the database experiences a failure, I want to be able to restore the system state from a backup, so that I do not lose my published content.
requirements: R1: Automate daily database backups to secure off-site storage.
R2: Provide a documented, scripted restoration path that has been executed and verified in staging.

slices.title: Automated Backup Configuration
slices.jtbd: When implementing the build/deploy for this epic, I want to script daily backups, so that the Data Protection and Recovery outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the production database service
When the scheduled cron task executes
Then a pg_dump archive is securely pushed to off-site storage

slices.title: Restoration Path Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to ensure backups can actually be restored, so that the Data Protection and Recovery outcome is achieved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a populated backup archive
When the restore script is executed against a fresh test container
Then the database state is successfully fully recovered
